question_vi: Fast-forward merge vs no-ff merge: khác nhau gì? GitHub mặc định dùng cái nào và tại sao team nên chủ động chọn?
question_en: Fast-forward merge vs no-ff merge: what is the difference? What does GitHub use by default and why should teams choose deliberately?
answer_vi:
**Fast-forward merge** (mặc định khi có thể): nếu branch hiện tại là ancestor trực tiếp của branch cần merge, git chỉ di chuyển HEAD pointer lên — không tạo merge commit. History linear.

```bash
git checkout main
git merge feature/login  # nếu main chưa có commit mới → fast-forward
# History: A - B - C(feature) ← HEAD/main
```

**No-ff merge** (`--no-ff`): luôn tạo merge commit dù có thể fast-forward.
```bash
git merge --no-ff feature/login
# History: A - B - M ← merge commit
#               \
#                C(feature)
```

**Trade-offs:**
- Fast-forward: history clean, dễ `git log --oneline`, nhưng mất context "đây là feature branch"
- No-ff: thấy rõ feature grouping, dễ revert cả feature (`git revert -m 1 <merge-commit>`), nhưng log lộn xộn

**GitHub**: repo mới bật sẵn cả 3 merge method (merge commit / squash / rebase) — vào Settings tắt bớt để ép team dùng 1 strategy thống nhất. Nút merge của PR không bao giờ fast-forward — luôn tạo commit mới (merge commit, hoặc commit squash/rebase).

**Recommendation**: enforce squash merge (1 commit/PR) để main history clean, hoặc no-ff nếu cần preserve feature grouping. Đừng mix strategies trong 1 repo
answer_en:
**Fast-forward merge** (default when possible): if the current branch is a direct ancestor of the branch being merged, git simply moves the HEAD pointer forward — no merge commit created. History is linear.

```bash
git checkout main
git merge feature/login  # if main has no new commits → fast-forward
# History: A - B - C(feature) ← HEAD/main
```

**No-ff merge** (`--no-ff`): always creates a merge commit even when fast-forward is possible.
```bash
git merge --no-ff feature/login
# History: A - B - M ← merge commit
#               \
#                C(feature)
```

**Trade-offs:**
- Fast-forward: clean history, easy `git log --oneline`, but loses context that "this was a feature branch"
- No-ff: clearly shows feature grouping, easy to revert an entire feature (`git revert -m 1 <merge-commit>`), but log becomes cluttered

**GitHub**: new repos have all 3 merge methods enabled by default (merge commit / squash / rebase) — use Settings to disable the ones you do not want and force one consistent strategy. The PR merge button never fast-forwards — it always creates a new commit (a merge commit, or a squash/rebase commit).

**Recommendation**: enforce squash merge (1 commit/PR) for a clean main history, or no-ff if feature grouping must be preserved. Do not mix strategies within one repo
